This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day, Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under: Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice R.Devdas And Hon'Ble Mr Justice G Basavaraja Oral Judgment (Per: Hon'Ble Mr Justice G Basavaraja) This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short), has been filed by the appellant-claimant being NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 22.03.2019 passed in MVC No.159/2017 by the Court of Prl. District Judge & MACT, Raichur, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal', for short). 2. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal. 3.
texts.facts: The facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that, on 29.03.2016 the injured petitioner Chinna Reddy @ Channareddy was proceeding as a pillion rider on TVS motorcycle Chinna Reddy @ Channareddy vs Gohappa And Ors on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140842566/ 2 bearing registration No.MH-12/DP-6913 and the vehicle was ridden by one Govind Rathod, who was in search of his missing son. When the said rider was riding the motorcycle in a very cautious manner at moderate speed on Manvi-Raichur main road, near Kapagal Village, Channabasaveshwar Petrol Bunk, due to negligent parking lorry bearing registration No.KA-36/4442 on the middle of the road by its driver respondent No.1 without any indication and without taking any precautionary measures, and due to NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB darkness, the rider of the motorcycle hit the parked lorry from back side. As a result of which, they fell and sustained grievous injuries. Govind Rathod the rider of the vehicle died in the Government Hospital, Manvi and injured initially took treatment at Government Hospital, Manvi and thereafter he was shifted to Basava Hospital, Raichur. The petitioner was shifted to Yashoda Hospital, Hyderabad and was admitted an inpatient in the said hospital from 30.03.2016 to 09.04.2016. Later, he admitted to St.Mary's Hospital, Bellary for follow up treatment. It is stated that as on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged about 41 years, doing agriculture work and earning Rs.15,000/-. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he has been permanently disabled and lost source of income, causing dent to him financially, mentally and physically. Hence, he preferred a claim petition seeking compensation. 4. After service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 did not appear, hence they were placed ex-parte. The NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB respondent No.3 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim petition and sought for dismissal of the petition. 5. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration. 6. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, next friend of petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and also examined one Doctor as PW.2 and got marked 82 documents as Exs.P1 to P82. On the other hand, respondent No.2-Insurer examined its official as RW.1 and got marked four documents as Exs.R1 to R4. 7. The Tribunal, after recording the evidence and considering the material on record, allowed the petition in part with costs and awarded compensation of Rs.7,45,880/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition until realization. The tribunal also fastened contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner to an extent of 50%. Being dissatisfied with the NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner has filed the present appeal seeking enhancement of compensation amount and also questioning the contributory negligence of 50% fastened on the claimant/petitioner. The said judgment and award passed by the Tribunal was challenged by the Insurance Company before this Court in MFA No.201020/2017 and the same came to be dismissed by the learned Single Judge vide order dated 09.03.2021.
texts.arguments: To fortify his submissions, the NC: 2024:KHC-K:9587-DB learned Counsel has relied on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mohammed Siddique and Another Vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company supports the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, contending that the same does not call for any interference. Further, he has not disputed the judgment dated 09.03.2021 passed by the learned Single Judge in MFA No.201020/2017 dismissing the appeal filed by the Insurance Company, which was also arising out of the same accident and the same is not challenged.
